topic: The AI Search Shift: Google vs Perplexity
description: A timeline comparison of how AI-first search interfaces rewired the traffic and product momentum behind Google Search—while Perplexity emerged from a late-2022 launch into a fast-growing “answer-first” challenger.

instagram_caption:
🚀 The AI Search Shift: Google’s “10 Blue Links” vs Perplexity’s answer-first sprint

For years, Google Search was the gravity well. In 2018 it sat around **$146B** (search monetization proxy), climbing to **$184B by 2022**—steady, dominant, and basically the default way humans “find stuff.” But then the expectations changed.

In **2022**, ChatGPT arrived and rewired the question people ask: less “show me results,” more “answer me.” That shift didn’t crush Google overnight—2023 still looks strong at **~$192B**—but it quietly exposed the weakness of keyword-first experiences. Users didn’t just want *links*. They wanted *decisions*: summarized, contextual, and fast.

That’s where Perplexity enters the story. It starts at **$0 in 2018–2021**, then shows up at **~$0.03B in 2022**—barely a blip, then suddenly impossible to ignore. By **2023**, Perplexity is estimated at **~$1.10B**, and it rockets again to **~$3.60B in 2024**. In **2025**, it’s projected/estimated at **~$6.80B**, riding the wave of “answer UI” with citations and fast synthesis.

Meanwhile, the race sprawled beyond Google. Microsoft’s Bing & Copilot moves from **~$38B (2022)** to **~$41B (2023)**, then **~$45B (2024)** and **~$48B (2025)**. And Meta’s AI-driven discovery flywheel keeps turning—**~$150B (2022)** to **~$165B (2023)**, **~$185B (2024)**, **~$205B (2025)**—because when people stop “searching” and start “discovering,” ads follow attention.

📌 Here’s the tension: Google still grows, but the *center of interaction* is moving. A new interface is winning—even if the old engine hasn’t crashed yet.

**Question:** If you could only use ONE format for everyday questions in 2026—classic search, answer-first assistants, or social discovery—which would you pick?
